rows.en: On my way back from the bathroom.

ghs.en: I had a random encounter with Tomoki.
ghs.assessment: 遭遇した simply says the narrator encountered Tomoki. 'Random encounter' adds explicit video-game terminology.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I run into Tomoki.'

highlights.text: I had a random encounter with Tomoki.

rows.jp: 「わはは、授業さぼってしまったよ。授業中の廊下って独特の世界って感じだよな」
rows.en: “Wahaha. I ended up skipping class. The hallways during lessons feel like a world of their own, don't they?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wahahah, we're totally cutting classes! You can just feel the uniqueness of the world that is a school corridor while classes are in session!"
ghs.assessment: The narrator says he himself skipped class. 'We're totally cutting classes' makes Tomoki jointly responsible and changes a completed lapse into a shared ongoing action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ha ha, I ended up skipping class.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wahahah, we're totally cutting classes! You can just feel the uniqueness of the world that is a school corridor while classes are in session!"

ghs.assessment: 虚しい describes the performance as hollow or dispiriting. 'Pointless' instead judges its utility.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's depressing, so stop...'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "It's pointless, just drop it..."

rows.jp: 「空転してこそ今時の僕らだ」
rows.en: “We're the youth of today precisely because we spin our wheels.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "We're just revving those engine these days, us young boys."
ghs.assessment: 空転 is the metaphor of spinning one's wheels. 'Revving those engine' has incorrect number agreement, while 'us young boys' adds a gendered self-label absent from the line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Spinning our wheels is what people our age do.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "We're just revving those engine these days, us young boys."

ghs.assessment: The direct address requires normal question punctuation and clause order. 'Easygoing aren't you' omits the comma and question mark.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You're carefree, aren't you, Taichi?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Easygoing aren't you, Taichi."

rows.jp: 「もうサイコマンの続きは読めないんだぞ」
rows.en: “You know we can never read the rest of Psycho Man.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Now I can never read how Psychoman continues no more."
ghs.assessment: The source says they can no longer read the continuation. 'Can never ... no more' uses a double negative that can reverse the meaning.
ghs.remedy: Use 'We'll never get to read the rest of Psychoman now.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Now I can never read how Psychoman continues no more."

ghs.assessment: 乾いた笑い is a dry, mirthless laugh. 'Parched' ordinarily describes extreme thirst and is not the established English emotional collocation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A dry laugh.'

highlights.text: A parched laugh.

ghs.assessment: The speaker label misspells Taichi as 'Tachi.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Taichi.'

highlights.text: Tachi: "...so it seems."

rows.jp: 友貴より早く読んで展開を教えることはできないんだな。
rows.en: I would never again get ahead of Tomoki and tell him what happened next.

ghs.en: Now I can't read ahead of Tomoki and spoil him anymore.

rows.en: “So what are you doing at school?”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "So, school, what'cha dying to do here?"
ghs.assessment: The source asks what brings him to school. 'Dying to do' adds eagerness and asks what activity he wants rather than his reason for coming.
ghs.remedy: Use 'So, what brings you to school?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "So, school, what'cha dying to do here?"

rows.jp: 「イノセンス・ライセンスを所持する俺なんかは、世界に取り残された十代の脆弱な心の機微を演出するため、通学するという日常的習慣を繰り返すことで」
rows.en: “As one who holds an Innocence License, I repeat the everyday ritual of going to school so I can stage the fragile inner life of a teenager left behind by the world—”

ghs.en: {}Taichi: "As a possessor of an Innocence License, for the purpose of acting out the sensitive and brittle heart of a teenager that was left behind in this world, I am going to depict that nihility of the soul that I should perhaps better call its automatic module via the repetition of the ordinary routine that is a commute to school."

rows.jp: 「精神の虚無というか自動的部分を描き出そうとしているわけだけどさ」
rows.en: “—and thereby depict the void in the psyche, or rather, its automatic element.”

rows.jp: 「十代の先鋭的な部分ばかりにとらわれた思想だね」
rows.en: “That's an ideology obsessed solely with the radical edge of adolescence.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "That's an idea that's all slave of a teenager's radicalist module."
ghs.assessment: The source critiques a worldview fixated only on the cutting-edge or radical aspects of adolescence. 'All slave of a teenager's radicalist module' is ungrammatical and invents a mechanistic module.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That worldview is fixated only on adolescence's most radical edge.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "That's an idea that's all slave of a teenager's radicalist module."

rows.jp: 「まだ熱血甲子園君だっていっぱいいるんだよ」
rows.en: “There are still plenty of hot-blooded Koshien hopefuls left.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "There's still lots of Hot Blooded Koshien-kun out there, you know."
ghs.assessment: The baseball-archetype label should use standard Hepburn Kōshien. 'Koshien' leaves the long vowel unmarked, and singular 'kun' conflicts with the many people referenced.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There are still plenty of hot-blooded Kōshien types out there.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "There's still lots of Hot Blooded Koshien-kun out there, you know."

rows.jp: 「あ、彼らはポストモダンとか言ってる連中のなかでは観察価値のある人間って見なされてないから」
rows.en: “Oh, the postmodern crowd doesn't consider them human beings worth observing.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, but among those of us who use words such as 'postmodern', they would not be considered as humans with any observational worth."
ghs.assessment: The source refers to people who talk about postmodernism from the outside. 'Those of us' makes the speaker a member of that group, while 'humans with observational worth' is an unidiomatic recasting of people worth observing.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Among the people who talk about postmodernism, they aren't considered worth observing.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, but among those of us who use words such as 'postmodern', they would not be considered as humans with any observational worth."

ghs.assessment: The source gives the narrator's dismissive hand wave as an action. 'Flapping wave of the hand' is a subjectless noun phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I wave a hand dismissively.'

highlights.text: Flapping wave of the hand.

ghs.assessment: だろー seeks agreement: 'Right?' 'Can I!' instead asks about the speaker's ability and is punctuated as an exclamation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Right?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wahahahahah, can I!"

rows.jp: 毒舌な友貴は好むのだ。

ghs.assessment: The source says sharp-tongued Tomoki likes black jokes. 'Sharp-tongued Tomoki's favorite' is a possessive noun fragment and omits the act of liking.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Sharp-tongued Tomoki enjoys that kind of thing.'

highlights.text: Sharp-tongued Tomoki's favorite.

rows.jp: 「太一のおかげで久しぶりに笑ったよ」
rows.en: “Thanks to you, I laughed for the first time in ages.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Haven't laughed thanks to you in a while, Taichi."
ghs.assessment: The source says Tomoki laughed for the first time in a while thanks to Taichi. 'Haven't laughed thanks to you in a while' says Taichi has prevented or failed to cause laughter.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Thanks to you, I laughed for the first time in ages.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Haven't laughed thanks to you in a while, Taichi."

ghs.en: Taichi: "Very glad to be up to the task."

rows.jp: 「つまみ食い大王が参加してないおかげで順調だよ」
rows.en: “Going smoothly, now that King Snack-Thief isn't participating.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Thanks to the non-participation of the Great King of Foodsnatchers, fine."
ghs.assessment: The source is a complete reply that things are going smoothly because the Great King of Snacking is absent. The English ends with the detached adjective 'fine.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's going smoothly, thanks to the Great King of Snacking not taking part.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Thanks to the non-participation of the Great King of Foodsnatchers, fine."

rows.jp: 「太一のとこは明日になると思う」

ghs.en: Tomoki: "I think I'll hit your place tomorrow, Taichi."

rows.jp: 暑苦しい笑顔、白い歯、立てた親指をガッとぶつけあう。
rows.en: With sweltering grins, flashing white teeth, we slammed our raised thumbs together.

ghs.en: A lively exchange with a sweltering smile, white teeth, and raised thumb.
ghs.assessment: The source describes the pair forcefully bumping their raised thumbs together amid exaggerated smiles and white teeth. 'A lively exchange' omits that central contact action, and singular 'thumb' conflicts with the pair.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With overheated smiles and flashing white teeth, we smack our raised thumbs together.'

highlights.text: A lively exchange with a sweltering smile, white teeth, and raised thumb.

rows.en: “Have you been showing up to club?”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Are you going to go to club?"

rows.jp: 「いや、つまみ食い大王だから参加拒否されたじゃん……おまえに」
rows.en: “No. King Snack-Thief was banned from participating... by you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nah, being the Great King of Foodsnatchers means my participation was rejected wasn't it... by you."
ghs.assessment: The source gives a coherent reminder that Tomoki rejected his participation. 'My participation was rejected wasn't it... by you' lacks the comma and question structure needed to attach the delayed agent.
ghs.remedy: Use 'No. You rejected me because I'm the Great King of Snacking, remember?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Nah, being the Great King of Foodsnatchers means my participation was rejected wasn't it... by you."

ghs.en: Words stagnate but for a moment.
ghs.assessment: 寸刻、言いよどむ says he hesitates for a brief moment. 'Words stagnate' turns speech hesitation into stationary language and uses an unnatural collocation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'He hesitates for a moment.'

highlights.text: Words stagnate but for a moment.

rows.en: “...I mean the one on the roof.”

ghs.assessment: The source means the club on the rooftop. 'The one on the rooftop's' ends with a possessive marker but supplies nothing possessed.
ghs.remedy: Use '...I mean the one on the rooftop.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...the one on the rooftop's."

rows.jp: 「あー、あんま出てないなぁ……いろいろあって」
rows.en: “Ah, not much lately... Things came up.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, I ain't really showing up... many reasons."
ghs.assessment: The explanation is that he has not attended much because various things happened. 'Many reasons' is a detached noun phrase rather than a causal clause.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ah, I haven't been going much... Various things came up.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, I ain't really showing up... many reasons."

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Well, that should be for the best, should it."
ghs.assessment: The source tentatively says that may be for the best. 'That should be for the best, should it' uses a malformed tag question with reversed polarity.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Well, maybe that's for the best.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Well, that should be for the best, should it."

ghs.assessment: いいよ、うん is a self-reassuring 'It's fine. Yeah.' 'Best, yes' incorrectly carries the adjective from the preceding translation into this separate line.
ghs.remedy: Use '...It's fine. Yeah.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...best, yes."

rows.jp: 背を向けて、友貴は立ち去る。
rows.en: Tomoki turned his back and walked away.

ghs.en: Turning his back to me, Tomoki departs.
Quite an odd behavior we had here.
ghs.assessment: The narrator observes that Tomoki was acting strangely. 'Quite an odd behavior we had here' makes the behavior shared, uses the wrong article, and removes Tomoki as its subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'He was acting strangely.'

highlights.text: Quite an odd behavior we had here.
